author: Nelev
body:
The opening message was a hardcoded `MESSAGES` array in `page.tsx`, so the UI rendered a greeting the backend knew nothing about. `GET /init?user=` now returns it, and the page reads it at request time.

## Backend

`GET /init?user=<id>` returns `{"messages": [{"role": "assistant", "text": "Hi <id>, how can I help you?"}]}`.

## Frontend

`Home` becomes an async Server Component and awaits the fetch on the server: no CORS preflight, no empty-list flash before the first paint. The uncached fetch marks the route dynamic, so `loading.tsx` covers the wait — it mirrors the page's rails exactly, and the shared `ChatHeader` keeps the two from drifting into a layout shift on swap.

The message shape moves to `model/ChatMessage` and the prop is `text` rather than `content`, matching the JSON the endpoint returns instead of renaming it at the boundary.

The backend origin comes from `API_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8000`). It has no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix on purpose — the module is imported only from a Server Component, so it never reaches the browser bundle.

## Known gaps

- The user is a hardcoded patient id, in one constant so there is a single place to change when auth lands. It is interpolated into the greeting as-is, so the page currently shows the raw id — the endpoint has no display name to work with yet.
- `user` has no length constraint, so `/init?user=` yields `"Hi , how can I help you?"`. Left as-is rather than pinned by a test, since it is a gap rather than a decision.

## Testing

Three tests in `tests/test_main.py` cover the greeting, the round trip of an opaque id, and that a missing `user` is a 422 rather than a 500. They reuse the existing ASGITransport client fixture, so they need no database.

- `pytest`: 66 passed
- `ruff check`: clean
- `yarn lint` and `yarn tsc --noEmit`: clean
